questions.q: The degree of unsaturation of nitrobenzene, C₆H₅NO₂, is
questions.explain: Drop O and remove one H for the N: C₆H₄, so DU = (14 − 4)/2 = 5 (benzene ring 4 + N=O 1).

questions.q: What is the degree of unsaturation of C₉H₉NO₄?
questions.explain: Ignore the four O atoms and subtract one H for N, giving C₉H₈; DU = (20 − 8)/2 = 6. A fractional answer for a neutral molecule always signals an error.

questions.q: The degree of unsaturation of the pyridinium ion, C₅H₆N⁺, is
questions.explain: Convert the ion to its neutral parent by removing the extra H⁺: pyridine C₅H₅N, which gives DU = 4. Applying a blanket 'positive charge: add H' rule is the trap.

questions.q: A compound C₆H₁₀ takes up only one mole of H₂ on catalytic hydrogenation. Its structure contains
options: Two rings and no π bond
questions.explain: C₆H₁₀ has DU = (14 − 10)/2 = 2. Hydrogenation adds H₂ to π bonds but does not open ordinary rings, so one mole of H₂ means one C=C plus one ring, as in cyclohexene.
